title: How Do the Latest Black Sea Attacks Affect Global Food Security?
summary_en: For the first time since 2022, attacks on agricultural infrastructure and cargo vessels are limiting grain exports from Russia and Ukraine at the same time. CSIS experts examine the latest attacks, their food-security impacts, and how the Iran war is worsening the crisis.

title: Hormuz Needs a Community, Not a Condominium
summary_en: A deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz that sidelines Gulf states would entrench coercion and invite a new conflict. Postwar Europe offers a better model: a shared governance mechanism that dilutes leverage and fosters long-term cooperation.
title_cn: Hormuz Needs a Community, Not a Condominium

title: The Billion-Dollar Chip: Who Can Afford to Design the Future?
summary_en: As the cost of designing leading-edge chips approaches $1 billion, frontier semiconductor design is becoming accessible to fewer firms. The United States must reduce the underlying cost of design to preserve innovation and competitiveness across critical industries.
title_cn: The Billion-Dollar Chip: Who Can Afford to Design the Future?

title: Adapting to the New Terrorism Landscape 25 Years After 9/11
summary_en: Post-9/11 counterterrorism efforts made large, foreign-directed attacks harder to execute. Stopping the terrorist threat that remains today requires a new approach.
